六级大纲词汇 · 20英文原文

The Door with No Sign

没有招牌的那扇门 · 580 词 · 6 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A newspaper wanted Tess to investigate a notorious market for heroin and cocaine. Its editor had already planned a headline about a dealer's notoriety. Tess's first interview was with a young man who had spent months hiding an addiction. He feared an arrest would aggravate his situation and preoccupy his family. To him an addiction he could not control felt like a perpetual ordeal. When he became suicidal, a friend had brought him to a clinic with no sign on its door. The editor called the clinic a side issue. Tess wondered why the young man had mentioned it before he mentioned the dealer.

2At the clinic a psychiatrist showed her an anonymous survey. Its demographic table listed each patient's age range and neighborhood. His exact figures could identify him. Tess could cite the aggregate numbers instead. A physician had also tracked the aggravation of physical symptoms after missed appointments. Some people had stopped attending because they feared being treated as offenders. No one could infer from the figures alone how many had hitherto stayed away.

3Tess interviewed a nurse who had worked in psychiatry for twenty years. The nurse described a vicious cycle. Pain and shame increased isolation, which made patients less willing to seek help. An obsessive fear about a confidential record could inhibit conversation. In one interview the nurse asked about that obsession before she asked what the patient had taken. One patient had spent a morning in solitary silence outside the clinic. Tess could not tell how many people still faced that kind of alienation. A compassionate greeting helped elicit what she needed. It did not cure the illness. It gave the nurse enough information to arrange a proper assessment.

4A councillor wanted to outlaw several substances sold near the market. He called the clinic too lenient and suggested naming patients in a deterrent campaign. Tess asked what would happen to someone who disclosed an addiction in confidence. He accused her of defending vice. In his view a more punitive policy would intimidate users into staying away. She asked him to look at the dates. There had been no increase in reports of crime around the clinic. A police officer confirmed that a separate operation could still prosecute dealers without using the clinic's patient list.

5Tess removed the street description and a quotation that gave the dealer a seductive glamour. In its place she used a short account of how a first visit worked. It explained how agitation and dread could build during a long wait. The editor said a lurid opening could lure more readers than this sober account. A thriller would distort the young man's experience. Tess showed him the young man's original account. He had described his first interview as an ordeal, then said the quiet greeting had mattered more than the words used to describe his condition. They kept the greeting.

6After publication a reader accused Tess of trying to appease people who sold drugs. Another said her son had recognized his own fear in the piece and sought an appointment. Tess could not infer a lasting effect from one letter. She asked the clinic what had changed. Evening appointments had become free, a noteworthy change for someone working late. The clinic put a sign on the door. The young man returned to show her the sign. It gave a time and the name of someone who would answer. That was all he had wanted to know when he first came in.

六级大纲词汇 · 20中文译文

没有招牌的那扇门

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1报社让苔丝调查一个声名狼藉的海洛因和可卡因交易点。编辑已经想好了标题，要写那个出了恶名的毒贩。苔丝最先采访一名隐瞒药物成瘾几个月的年轻人。他怕被捕会让处境更糟，也让家人一直担心。对他来说，无法控制的成瘾是一场没完没了的折磨。他有了自杀念头时，朋友把他带到一家门上没有招牌的诊所。编辑觉得诊所只是枝节。苔丝却想知道，为什么年轻人先说起那扇门，再说到毒贩。

2诊所的一名精神科医生给她看了一份匿名调查。人口统计表列出每名病人的年龄段和居住地区。如果报出这名年轻人的确切数据，别人可能认出他。苔丝可以引用汇总数字。一名医生还记录了病人错过预约后身体症状加重的情况。有些人怕被当成违法者，就不再来了。单凭表格，谁也推不出此前有多少人一直没来求助。

3苔丝采访了一位在精神科工作二十年的护士。护士说，疼痛和羞耻让人更孤立，越孤立又越不愿求助，形成了恶性循环。对保密记录反复担忧，连普通对话都可能说不下去。有一次，护士先问病人究竟在担心什么，再问她用过什么药。一名病人曾独自坐在诊所外，沉默了一整个早晨。苔丝不知道还有多少人有这种疏离感。一句体谅的问候让病人开口说出需要，也让护士获得足够的信息来安排评估。

4一名议员想禁止市场附近出售几种物质。他嫌诊所太宽容，建议在警示宣传中公开病人的姓名。苔丝问，那些在保密前提下承认成瘾的人会怎么样。议员指责她替恶习辩护，还认为惩罚严一点，就能吓得用药者不再靠近。苔丝让他对照日期。诊所周边的犯罪报案并没有增加。一位警官也证实，另外展开调查，仍可以起诉毒贩，无需动用诊所的病人名单。

5苔丝删掉了街道描述和一句把毒贩写得很有吸引力的话，改用一小段交代第一次就诊的过程。那段话说明等待太久为什么会加重焦躁和恐惧。编辑说，耸动的开头比这样的平实叙述更能吸引读者。苔丝给他看年轻人的原话。年轻人说第一次谈话对自己是场煎熬，最后真正记住的，是护士轻声打的招呼。把他的经历写成惊险故事会走样。他们留下了那句问候。

6文章发出后，有人指责苔丝在讨好卖毒品的人。另一位读者说，她儿子在报道中认出了自己的恐惧，主动约了看诊。苔丝无法从一封信判断长远影响。她去问诊所做了哪些改动。晚间预约已经免费，这对下班晚的人很重要。诊所还在门上挂了块小牌子。年轻人回来给她看，上面有接诊时间和负责人的名字。那正是他第一次来时最想知道的事。
